correctness.rationale: For arbitrary interior pi,c,s,p1,p2,p3 with c!=s, the full observation law yields r2=s*p2, r3=s*p3, h2=z2/s, h3=z3/s and T=c/s+(s-c). Using z3=c+(s-c)z2, the two affine constraints solve delta=(T-h3)/(1-h2), b=T-delta, s=delta/(1-b), c=bs, pi=(s*h2-c)/delta, and all three p. Denominators 1-h2=delta*(1-pi)/s and 1-b=delta/s cannot vanish. A continuous two-season alias family and equal-transition indefinite alias establish sharp necessity. Exact Fraction implementation independently sums all observation histories and passes 554 interior tuples plus alias witnesses.

originality.rationale: The assessed finding is the global rational inverse from an eight-cell three-season law with unrestricted p1,p2,p3 and initial pi, together with a sharp two-occasion insufficiency and singular equal-transition boundary. Classical dynamic-occupancy literature does not settle this special inverse in the inspected accessible material. The generic three-observation HMM theorem of An, Hu and Shum assumes homogeneous emissions; Liu and Culpepper heterogeneous-emission theorem imposes strict emission positivity and neighboring equal emissions and stationary hidden initialization, all of which fail for the claimed arbitrary-p three-season model. Relevant literature and indexed scientific records did not identify a stronger encompassing theorem; incomplete access to the original ecological methods article and uncatalogued inverse-HMM papers are acknowledged.
residual_risks: Historical MacKenzie et al. (2003) full text could not be materially read despite open-access attempt; unresolved historical literature may have an equivalent inverse.
A theorem for partially observed two-state Markov chains not indexed by ecological or HMM vocabulary may cover this restricted structural-zero model.
Uniqueness fails exactly at c=s and ill-conditioning may become extreme near that boundary; practical finite-sample estimability is unstudied.

value.rationale: For a fixed-colonization-and-persistence ecological monitoring model with no within-season repeat visits and drifting seasonal detectability, three surveys are both necessary and sufficient for structural recovery of hidden dynamics and all individual detection rates. The sharp equal-transition exception distinguishes real unobservability from merely low sample size. The result provides an explicit design benchmark and transparent inversion, and does not claim practical statistical consistency or robustness to site heterogeneity.
